payload.question_text: Which field is commonly included in an invoice schema?

options.error_type: Confuses invoice fields with audio output
options.rationale: A transcript is an output that can come from audio analysis. It is not a common invoice schema field.
options.better_fit: Use this when analyzing a recorded call and reviewing its written transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: The accounts worker would look for call content instead of the invoice's final amount.
feedback.instructional: Invoice schemas contain invoice details such as totals, dates, customers, and items.

options.error_type: Confuses invoice fields with meeting fields
options.rationale: Remote attendees can be part of a meeting-image or video schema. They are not invoice details.
options.better_fit: Use this when analyzing attendance in a conference recording or conference-room image.

feedback.intrinsic: Attendance details would not help an accounts worker determine the amount due.
feedback.instructional: Choose fields that match the content being processed; invoice schemas focus on invoice information.

options.rationale: Invoice total is one of the common fields in an invoice schema. It represents the final invoice amount.

options.error_type: Confuses invoice fields with video fields
options.rationale: Location can be extracted from a meeting image or video. It is not a common invoice field.
options.better_fit: Use this when identifying the location shown in meeting media.

feedback.intrinsic: The worker would capture a meeting detail while the invoice total remains unaddressed.
feedback.instructional: Invoice schemas include financial and customer details, not meeting-location details.

payload.explanation: Correct. Invoice total is a common field in an invoice schema and gives the final amount.

payload.question_text: Which tasks can basic OCR do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: OCR can read a vendor name, but basic OCR does not understand what the name means. Identifying it as the vendor uses meaning-based extraction.
options.better_fit: Use this when a value must be mapped to a VendorName field even when labels vary.

feedback.intrinsic: A vendor name may appear in the readable text without being identified as the vendor.
feedback.instructional: OCR reads words; semantic extraction maps values to fields by meaning.

options.text: Read text on a scanned page
options.rationale: OCR can read printed text from scanned pages. This is its core purpose.

options.text: Link each price to its item
options.error_type: Confuses OCR with nested schema fields
options.rationale: Basic OCR does not understand relationships between words or values. Nested item fields preserve the price, quantity, and total for each item.
options.better_fit: Use this when an Items collection must keep each product's details together.

feedback.intrinsic: A worker could see all the prices but not know which product each one belongs to.
feedback.instructional: Use a collection with nested fields to preserve item-to-price relationships.

options.rationale: OCR converts visible receipt text into digital text. Digital text can be searched.

payload.explanation: Correct. Basic OCR can read printed text and make that text searchable, but it does not interpret its meaning.

payload.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The idea that nested details belong to individual item records may become unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name Items, identify it as a collection, then state that it contains item records with nested fields.

payload.correct_answer: Items is a collection of item records with nested fields
payload.explanation: The order identifies Items first, then explains that it contains multiple records and that those records contain nested fields. This structure preserves each item's related values.

payload.question_text: Mapping Invoice # to InvoiceNumber by meaning is called ___.

parts.text: Mapping Invoice # to InvoiceNumber by meaning is called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The invoice number may be readable but not recognized as belonging in InvoiceNumber when the label changes.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose semantic extraction for meaning-based mapping. OCR reads text, and schema-based extraction defines the broader field-and-structure approach.

payload.explanation: Semantic field extraction maps a value to a schema field by what the value represents. OCR reads visible text, while schema-based extraction is the broader approach for extracting defined fields and structure.

payload.question_text: A buyer's invoice lists a bike, a helmet, and a shirt. The accounts worker must keep each product's details connected. What should the Items structure preserve for each product? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Each item record can include its own unit price. This keeps the price connected to the correct product.
Each item record can include its own quantity ordered. The quantity stays associated with that product.
Each item record can include its own line item total. This preserves the amount for that individual item.

options.error_type: Confuses separate item records with one flat field
options.rationale: Each item record has its own item description. One shared description would not distinguish the bike, helmet, and shirt.
options.better_fit: Use one shared value only when the same single value truly applies to the whole invoice.

feedback.intrinsic: The worker could no longer tell which price, quantity, and total belong to each product.
feedback.instructional: Keep a separate record for every product, including that product's own description and nested values.

payload.explanation: Correct. Each item record preserves its own unit price, quantity ordered, and line item total.

payload.question_text: An invoice processor receives an invoice labeled “Invoice #” and must place its number in the InvoiceNumber field. Which approach should the processor use?

options.rationale: Semantic field extraction recognizes that Invoice # represents the invoice-number concept. It can therefore map the value to InvoiceNumber.

options.error_type: Chooses text reading without meaning mapping
options.rationale: Basic OCR can read Invoice # and its number. It does not map the number to InvoiceNumber by meaning.
options.better_fit: Use this when the goal is only to turn visible printed text into searchable digital text.

feedback.intrinsic: The label and number may be readable, but the number could remain unassigned to the intended field.
feedback.instructional: OCR reads the words; semantic field extraction recognizes what the number represents.

options.error_type: Chooses unstructured text instead of semantic mapping
options.rationale: A flat text field does not explain how Invoice # maps to the InvoiceNumber concept. The task requires meaning-based field mapping.
options.better_fit: Use this when only one simple text value is needed without a structured mapping decision.

feedback.intrinsic: The number could be stored as plain text without being identified as the invoice number.
feedback.instructional: Use semantic extraction to map the value to the correct schema field by meaning.

options.error_type: Chooses line-item structure instead of field mapping
options.rationale: An Items collection stores multiple product records and their nested details. It does not map an invoice reference number to InvoiceNumber.
options.better_fit: Use this when processing several ordered products with separate prices, quantities, and line totals.

feedback.intrinsic: The invoice reference could be treated like a product detail instead of a header field.
feedback.instructional: Items organizes line items; semantic extraction maps the invoice number to its proper field.

payload.explanation: Correct. Semantic field extraction recognizes that Invoice # and InvoiceNumber refer to the same invoice-number concept.

payload.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition can blur the difference between required information and its structure.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the schema, then state the information it describes, its extraction purpose, and its structure.

payload.correct_answer: A schema describes information to extract and its structure
payload.explanation: The order moves from the schema to its purpose, then completes that purpose with structure. Both what to extract and how to organize it are required parts of a schema.

payload.question_text: The invoice field for the amount charged for delivery is ___.

parts.text: The invoice field for the amount charged for delivery is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The delivery amount could be added to the wrong financial category.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use Shipping Charge for delivery. Tax is tax, subtotal is the amount before final charges, and Invoice total is the final amount.

payload.explanation: Shipping Charge identifies the delivery cost separately from tax, subtotal, and the final invoice total. These are distinct invoice amounts.

payload.question_text: An expense-processing team must capture vendor, customer, and total from every scanned invoice. What should the team define or use? Select all that apply.

options.error_type: Chooses text recognition without field structure
options.rationale: Basic OCR can read visible invoice text. It does not understand the business fields or relationships needed by the team.
options.better_fit: Use this when the only goal is to make printed invoice text searchable.

feedback.intrinsic: The team may receive readable words but still lack separate vendor, customer, and total values.
feedback.instructional: OCR is useful for text recognition; defined business fields need a schema and schema-based extraction.

options.error_type: Confuses searching text with extracting fields
options.rationale: Searching text can find words but does not define which values belong in required fields. The task needs structured vendor, customer, and total values.
options.better_fit: Use this when someone only needs to locate a word or phrase in readable text.

feedback.intrinsic: Different invoice layouts could make it hard to consistently capture the required details.
feedback.instructional: A search finds text; a schema-based approach extracts defined fields consistently.

options.rationale: The team needs to state which details are required, including vendor, customer, and total. A schema defines those fields and their structure.
Schema-based extraction captures the defined fields and their values. It goes beyond merely reading the invoice words.

payload.explanation: Correct. The team should define the required fields in a schema and use schema-based extraction to capture their values.

payload.question_text: The technology that reads printed text from a scanned receipt is ___.

parts.text: The technology that reads printed text from a scanned receipt is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The receipt text would not be identified as readable digital text by that term.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose OCR for reading visible printed text. Schema-based extraction defines fields, while semantic extraction maps values by meaning.

payload.explanation: OCR is the part that turns visible printed words in an image into editable, searchable digital text. Schema-based and semantic extraction add structure or meaning beyond text reading.

payload.question_text: An accounts clerk is processing an invoice and needs the final amount due. Which schema field should the clerk use?

options.rationale: Invoice subtotal is a separate invoice field. The final amount due is identified by Invoice total.
options.better_fit: Use this when the clerk needs the subtotal rather than the final amount.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk could report an amount before all final charges are included.
feedback.instructional: Choose Invoice total when the need is the final amount due.

options.error_type: Confuses one charge with final total
options.rationale: Tax is one component of invoice charges. It is not the invoice's final total.
options.better_fit: Use this when the clerk specifically needs the tax amount.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk would report only one charge instead of the complete amount due.
feedback.instructional: Tax and Invoice total are separate fields; the total is the final amount.

options.error_type: Confuses delivery charge with final total
options.rationale: Shipping Charge is the amount charged for delivery. It is not the complete invoice total.
options.better_fit: Use this when the clerk needs the delivery cost.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk would report the delivery fee rather than the full amount due.
feedback.instructional: Use Shipping Charge only for delivery; use Invoice total for the final amount.

options.rationale: Invoice total is the final amount due on the invoice. It is distinct from individual charges and the subtotal.

payload.explanation: Correct. Invoice total is the field for the final amount due.

payload.question_text: An expense-claim clerk needs to make text in scanned receipts searchable. Which capability should the clerk use?

options.error_type: Chooses meaning mapping instead of text recognition
options.rationale: Semantic extraction maps values to fields by meaning. The stated need is to read receipt text for searching.
options.better_fit: Use this when a value must be placed in a field despite a changed or missing label.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk may focus on field meanings before the receipt text has simply been made searchable.
feedback.instructional: For searchable visible text, start with basic OCR.

options.rationale: Basic OCR reads printed text from scanned receipt images. That text can then be searchable.

options.error_type: Chooses field design instead of text recognition
options.rationale: An invoice schema defines details such as vendor, tax, and total. It does not itself read printed receipt text.
options.better_fit: Use this when the clerk must extract specific invoice fields in a defined structure.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk would have a list of fields but not the readable receipt text needed for search.
feedback.instructional: A schema defines what to capture; OCR reads visible text.

options.error_type: Chooses invoice structure instead of text recognition
options.rationale: Items is a collection that holds several product records. It is not the capability for reading scanned text.
options.better_fit: Use this when each ordered product needs its own description, price, quantity, and line total.

feedback.intrinsic: Only product details would be organized, while other receipt text might remain unreadable for search.
feedback.instructional: An Items field organizes line items after relevant values are extracted.

payload.explanation: Correct. Basic OCR is suited to reading visible receipt text and making it searchable.
